_readme: The /onboard-new-client playbook as a chain definition, so the sequence survives a session ending halfway through it. The prose playbook commands/onboard-new-client.md remains the authority on what each step means and why it is ordered this way -- this file only carries the sequence, the decision points, and which steps must not be advanced past silently.
name: onboard-new-client
description: Stand up the documentation and config foundation of a new API/service or library project.

steps.purpose: Survey the project: manifests, stack, source roots; write survey.json for sign-off.
steps.decisionPoint: Has a human read the survey before it is used as the basis for everything downstream?
steps.checkpointReason: The survey is the root every later step hangs off; a wrong stack or source root read here is inherited silently by all of them.

steps.purpose: Scaffold the doc-role suite the declared projectKind expects (api, api-standard, production-readiness, ...), reverse-engineered from the codebase where the content already exists.
steps.decisionPoint: Is this a zero-docs project? A project whose expected roles already have documents skips this entirely.
steps.skipIf: The expected roles for this projectKind already have documents.
steps.checkpointReason: Generating a doc suite over one that already exists is destructive in a way nothing downstream would notice.

steps.purpose: Propose values for the scaffolded TODO config sections from code evidence; preview by default, applied only on approval.
steps.decisionPoint: Do the proposed values match what this project actually does, or is the code not yet readable enough to say?

steps.purpose: Record where the project starts, so later runs show direction of travel rather than a number with nothing to compare against.
